_comment: vehFeedback: the first vftable handover where slot ORDER could be wrong. Ten slots, and the
order the binary requires is nothing like alphabetical - so this is what actually exercises
the vtable-order fix in tools/genheaders.py. Check with:
The destructor is listed because porting it is what makes MSVC emit ??_7vehFeedback@@6B@ and
so triggers the handover. ??_GvehFeedback@@UAEPAXI@Z is NOT listed: asm.py picks the deleting
destructor up from handover.strip_procs, since MSVC generates it from the class definition
alone and it is declared in no header.
Five of the ten virtuals stay in the assembly on purpose - the C++ table then points partly
here and partly at 1999 code, which is what makes a ten-slot class portable a few functions at
a time. SetActuatorValue is among them until the fields at 0x18 and 0x1C are typed f32; see the
note at the top of vehfeedback.cpp.
